info.title: SIW -- Smol InterWebs
info.description: Offline fulltext search over the ZIM corpus this machine configured, served as JSON. One port answers the kernel routes (this document) and the console routes (`/state`, `/action`, `/mcp`, and the page itself). The engine's address is never a request parameter: the corpus, the port, the bind and the binary are the operator's act at the config. A request never names a host, a port, a directory or a binary. Responses are one JSON object always; failures carry `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` with the status that names the kind of failure. Credentials: loopback answers without any; a bind beyond loopback mandates a password, enforced at boot, and every route on the port then answers `401` until `Authorization: Basic` is right.

get.summary: The card a curious client reads first
get.description: What this is, and every route this server answers.

get.summary: The deployment's vital signs, read live
get.description: Is the engine answering, on what address is it actually bound, is that loopback-only, and how many books does it serve against how many the config picked. Never touches the internet.

200.description: Always 200 -- a down engine is `ok: false` with the facts, not an error status.

ok.description: true when the engine answered the probe

engine.description: host, port, up, bound_on, loopback_only, form, started_by_siw, catalog_problem

served.description: the engine's own catalog count; null when down or unreadable (never 0 for 'nobody looked')

drift.description: served vs configured set difference; null when down

get.description: `q` is required. `mode=global` (default) is the engine's merged ranking over everything served; `mode=grouped` asks each book its own question and answers with each book's best hit plus its hit count. `heal=0` refuses to start an engine as a side effect of a query. A zero-hit answer carries a `zero_hit` sentence that says what the zero does not mean.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to search for (AND across all terms). `query=` is accepted as a spelling of the same thing. Missing or blank is a 400.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: Global route only: comma/space-separated book-name substrings narrowing the selection. Refused with mode=grouped.

parameters.name: corpus
parameters.description: Global route only: family substring filter (e.g. 'wikipedia'). Refused with mode=grouped.

parameters.name: heal
parameters.description: 0/false/no refuses to start a down engine; the query then answers 503.

parameters.name: books
parameters.description: Grouped route only: comma/space-separated book names (file stems) -- the universe every named book answers out of. Unknown names are a 400.

zero_hit.description: empty when there were results; else the contract sentence for the kind of zero

book_errors.description: grouped route only: books whose own request failed

get.description: The directory listing with sizes, the pick, and (with `served=1`) what the running engine says it serves. The names printed here are the ones `books=` and `sources=` speak.

parameters.name: served
parameters.description: 1/true/yes adds the engine's own served names

whole_corpus.description: true when selected is null (nothing was narrowed)

get.summary: This server's OpenAPI document, as JSON
get.description: The document you are reading, answered by the server it describes. The file behind it is this repo's `docs/api.json` (overridable with `SIW_SPEC`).

get.summary: The console snapshot (the page's only read)
get.description: One JSON object with the whole truth the console page renders: server, engine, pending_apply, corpus, rows, tasks, notices. Answers fully with the engine down and never touches the internet. The field tables are `web/CONTRACT.md` section 1.

post.summary: One console verb and its args
post.description: `{"verb": str, "args": object}` in, one JSON object out: `{"ok": true, "result": {...}}` or `{"ok": false, "error": {"code", "message"}}`. The verb table is `web/CONTRACT.md` section 2. A same-origin check guards the POST: a body carrying a cross-origin `Origin` or `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` is refused without being run.

Three tools over the same service as everything else: `search`, `list_books`, `add_book`. A single JSON-RPC message in, one object out; a batch array in, an array out; a notification gets 202 with no body. Same-origin checks and credentials apply as on `/action`.

202.description: A notification was accepted; nothing to answer.

Error.description: One error shape everywhere: a code a machine can branch on, a sentence a person can act on.

Unauthorized.description: Credentials are configured and this request did not carry the right ones.
